gen_risks.description: Delay in recruiting required specialists (accountant, environmental, gender‑based violence, etc.) may postpone PIU set‑up and hinder project start‑up.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare a recruitment timetable, offer competitive contracts, and assign senior staff to monitor hiring progress.
gen_risks.evidence: CEMAC financing agreement (Section I.A.1b) requires appointment of specialists within 1 month of effective date.

gen_risks.description: Failure to customize accounting software within three months could impair financial tracking and reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Engage IT vendor early, set clear milestones, and conduct weekly progress reviews.
gen_risks.evidence: Financing agreements (e.g., CEMAC Section I.A.1c, Cameroon Section I.A.2b) mandate software customization within 3 months.

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays and weak contract management in fragile settings may cause cost overruns and missed deadlines.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, provide World Bank procurement training, and use flexible procurement methods for FCV contexts.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management; mitigation measures listed in section 64‑66.

gen_risks.description: Environmental hazards from construction and laboratory waste could affect surrounding communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement site‑specific ESMPs, follow the National Healthcare Waste Management Plan, and monitor waste disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental risks listed as substantial (sections 65‑66); waste, dust, emissions, occupational health mentioned.

gen_risks.description: Sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA/SH) risk due to increased community health workers and frontline staff.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct GBV/SEA risk assessments, recruit GBV specialists, and train all staff on SEA/SH protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: SEA/SH risks judged substantial; mitigation includes GBV specialists and action plans (sections 72‑73).

gen_risks.description: Political instability and conflict in Cameroon, CAR, Chad and RoC may disrupt service delivery and field activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop security risk assessments, maintain flexible implementation schedules, and coordinate closely with the Regional Coordination Committee.
gen_risks.evidence: Regional context notes conflict, FCV, IDPs (section 2‑3); annexes describe ongoing insecurity.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related shocks (floods, heat) could damage health facilities and increase disease burden.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design health‑facility upgrades with green, resilient standards and integrate climate data into surveillance systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change impacts described in sections 11‑12 and 37; green‑resilient approaches required.

gen_risks.description: Limited domestic fiscal space may reduce long‑term sustainability of health‑security investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support medium‑term expenditure frameworks, domestic resource mobilization, and public‑private partnership pilots.
gen_risks.evidence: Sustainability discussion highlights need for domestic budgeting and resource tracking (section 48‑49).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate cross‑border data sharing could limit early detection of outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen the RCC, finalize MoUs with WAHO, and adopt standardized data‑exchange protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Regional coordination mechanisms and MoU requirements outlined in sections 30‑31 and 57.

gen_risks.description: Gender gap in technical health workforce may reduce effectiveness of surveillance and response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement gender‑targeted recruitment, flexible training formats, and mentorship for women in epidemiology and veterinary fields.
gen_risks.evidence: Gender analysis and actions described in sections 75‑77.

gen_risks.description: Security threats to staff operating in conflict‑affected zones could cause injuries or project stoppage.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare Security Risk Assessments, Security Management Plans, and provide safety training and evacuation procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Security Risk Assessment and SMP to be prepared (section 73‑74).

gen_risks.description: Late submission of annual work plans and budgets may delay fund disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set internal deadlines 30 days before the World Bank deadline and use a tracking tool for approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require draft work plan by Nov 30 each year (Section I.C.1).

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement could exclude vulnerable groups and generate grievances.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy the Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conduct community consultations, and operate functional GRMs.
gen_risks.evidence: Stakeholder engagement risks noted in sections 65‑66 and 71‑74.

gen_risks.description: Substantial fiduciary risk (FM residual risk rated Substantial) may lead to mis‑allocation of funds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update FM manuals, recruit internal and external auditors, and conduct quarterly internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: FM residual risk assessed as Substantial; mitigation actions listed in sections 58‑60.

gen_risks.description: Limited procurement capacity (only one specialist) may hinder timely acquisition of goods and services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide procurement capacity‑building workshops and consider joint procurement to share workload.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement capacity described in section 62‑64; only one specialist and assistant noted.

gen_risks.description: Laboratory capacity shortfalls (accreditation, equipment) could delay pathogen detection and response.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement SLIPTA quality improvement, QMS mentoring, and procure essential equipment per sub‑component 2.2 plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Laboratory quality and capacity sub‑component details (sections 30‑33) and SLIPTA targets.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
